chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al-Khazzaz, from Abu Saeed Al-Mukari, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not upon the women to be loud with the Talbiyya.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: The ritual exclamation 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' recited during Hajj

ai.seo_question: Do women need to recite the Talbiyya aloud during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a specific jurisprudential distinction in the ritual of Hajj, noting that while men are encouraged to recite the Talbiyya aloud to manifest their devotion, women are exempt from this requirement of 'jahar' (audibility). This ruling reflects the broader Shia scholarly understanding of gender-specific nuances in ritual purity and public worship, emphasizing that the spiritual essence of the pilgrimage remains intact regardless of vocal volume.
